The smell of frites and the roar of engines – it can only be Spa!
The legendary Eau Rouge and Raidillon complex dominates the skyline, a constant reminder of the challenge this track presents.
The atmosphere is electric as the drivers prepare to tackle this iconic 7.004km circuit.
You can feel the history oozing from every corner of this place, a true cathedral of speed.
The fans are packed in tight, eager to witness another chapter in Spa's rich motorsport history.
The green hills surrounding the track offer a picturesque view, a stark contrast to the intensity of the racing.
Belgian flags are waving proudly as the national anthem plays, a stirring moment before the race begins.
The sheer scale of Spa is breathtaking, a proper old-school circuit that rewards bravery and precision.
historicalReferences: Think back to 1998, and that massive pile-up at the start – a stark reminder of how treacherous Spa can be, especially in the wet.
Michael Schumacher secured his seventh World Championship here in 2004, a fitting venue for such a momentous achievement.
Senna's masterful drive in the wet in '93 is still talked about today, a true display of car control and racecraft.
Remember Kimi Raikkonen's dominant victories here? He always seemed to have a special affinity for Spa.
The 2000 race saw Mika Hakkinen and Michael Schumacher battle wheel-to-wheel, culminating in that incredible overtake down the Kemmel Straight.
Spa has been a happy hunting ground for many British drivers, Damon Hill's win in '94 a particular highlight.
Let's not forget the controversial collision between Hamilton and Rosberg in 2014, a defining moment in their championship battle.
Spa has witnessed some incredible underdog stories, with smaller teams occasionally punching above their weight.
The Eau Rouge/Raidillon complex has been the scene of countless dramatic moments, both triumphs and tragedies.
This is where Leclerc got his first F1 victory in 2019, a very emotional day for the whole Ferrari team.
cornerCallouts: They're through La Source, that tight hairpin, and already accelerating hard towards Eau Rouge.
Through Eau Rouge and Raidillon, one of the most iconic corners in motorsport. Flat-out for most of these drivers.
Approaching Les Combes now, a crucial overtaking opportunity.
Down the Kemmel Straight they go, slipstreaming and DRS wide open.
Heavy braking now for Les Fagnes, a tricky chicane that can easily catch drivers out.
Negotiating Stavelot, a long right-hander that puts a lot of stress on the tires.
Pouhon, a high-speed left-hander that requires immense commitment and precision.
The final chicane, Bus Stop, a last-gasp opportunity to gain or lose a position before the start/finish line.
strategyPoints: Tire degradation is always a major factor here at Spa, especially on the medium and high-speed corners. Expect to see teams managing their tires carefully.
With a lap length of over 7km, the pit window is relatively short, meaning teams will need to be precise with their timing.
Fuel consumption is also a concern on this long circuit. Drivers will need to manage their fuel throughout the race.
The weather can change in an instant here in the Ardennes, so teams need to be prepared for anything.
An early safety car can completely change the complexion of the race, potentially opening up opportunities for alternative strategies.
Undercutting is often effective at Spa, with the long pit lane negating some of the time gained on track.
The tow down the Kemmel Straight is incredibly powerful, so track position is crucial in the closing stages of the race.
With so many high-speed sections, mechanical reliability is paramount. Any small issue can quickly become a race-ending problem.
weatherCommentary: The radar shows rain clouds approaching from the west. It looks like we could be in for a wet race.
The sun is shining now, but those clouds over the Ardennes mountains are a constant threat.
It's notoriously difficult to predict the weather at Spa. It can be raining on one part of the circuit and completely dry on another.
The air temperature is relatively cool, which could affect tire warm-up and performance.
The wind is picking up, which could make the high-speed corners even more challenging.
